item.title: Vitamin B12 (Cobalamin)
item.description:
What Is Vitamin B12?

Vitamin B12 (cobalamin) is a unique water-soluble vitamin containing cobalt at its center — the only vitamin containing a metal. B12 serves as a critical cofactor in just two major enzymes, but these enzymes catalyze absolutely essential reactions affecting energy production, DNA synthesis, neurological function, and the methylation cycle.

Biochemistry: B12 exists in several forms. The two primary active forms in the body are:

  • Methylcobalamin: Methyl donor form; directly supports the methylation cycle (methionine synthase)
  • Adenosylcobalamin (AdoCB12): Energy metabolism form; cofactor for methylmalonyl-CoA mutase

item.title: CoQ10
item.description:
What Is CoQ10?

Coenzyme Q10 (CoQ10), also called ubiquinone, is a naturally occurring coenzyme found in every cell in your body. It’s essential for:

  1. ATP Production — the energy currency of cells
  2. Antioxidant Defense — protecting cells from oxidative damage
  3. Cellular Signaling — regulating important biological processes

While your body produces CoQ10, production declines with age (dropping 50% by age 60) and is depleted by certain medications, particularly statins.

CoQ10 is especially critical for high-energy organs: the heart, brain, liver, and kidneys.
